newsitem.title: USA: Maine gov. supports targetting Midwest polluters.
newsitem.headline: Maine gov. supports targetting Midwest polluters.

text.p: Maine Gov. Angus King Tuesday said he supports a proposed regional boycott of electricty from Midwestern power plants that do not comply with strict clean air standards.

Massachusetts Attorney General Scott Harshbarger has urged 12 Northeast states and the District of Columbia to form a "Northeast Clean Air Compact." Harshbarger proposed that the states ban or place a surcharge on power from Midwestern states that allow dirty plants to operate.

King, who has writen a similar letter to other northeastern governors, has blamed polution from Midwestern power plants for much of Maine's difficulty in meeting federal air quality standards during the summer.

King has expressed the concern of many northeastern evironmental officials that pollution will increase as deregulation of the U.S. electric industry increases the demand of power from lower-cost coal-fired power plants.

"Fundamentally it just does not make comon sense to allow plants in the Midwest that don't meet environmental requirements of the rest of the country to gear up and double their output of power sending us lousy air at the same time," King told reporters.

The proposal for the Northeastern states banding together has drawn opposition from some Midwestern political leaders, and at least one New England environmental group has said it will oppose the plan.

"Basically what this is is an effort by the northeast states to band together... to point a finger at somebody else for a pollution problem that is in part caused by their own actions," said Rusty Russell, a staff attorney for the Conservation Law Foundation, told Maine Public Radio.
